scope: Synthetic PDF in Chromium using trusted CDP pen/touch and real mouse events; tests input classification, scrolling, coexistence and optional pen-only policy.
checks: trusted pen still creates text-bound PDF highlights
touch drag scrolls in text-markup mode without creating annotations
trusted pen starts ink and reports actual received pen input
touch scrolls an ink page while preserving every completed pen stroke
touch pans horizontally on a zoomed PDF without drawing
cancelled touch pan releases cleanly and the next gesture remains usable
touch during an active pen stroke neither scrolls nor interrupts the stroke
pen-only option refuses mouse drawing while continuing to accept a pen
policy rejection message clears after accepted pen input and after changing the setting
turning pen-only off restores Sidecar-style mouse fallback
native PDF save contains only the four intentional strokes and one highlight
pen-only preference survives reload while confirmed PDF handwriting remains intact
input settings close with Escape and an outside click
600-pixel input menu remains unclipped with a visible 44-pixel checkbox-label target
original PDF unchanged with trusted input and no browser errors or external requests
limitations: No physical Apple Pencil, iPadOS27, Sidecar, Safari or Electron build was exercised.
Browser-reported pointer types are verified; this does not identify the physical device or prove operating-system palm rejection.
